subject: EmberStack post-incident readout and remediation roadmap
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Kim <lara.kim@emberstack.com>, EmberStack Ops <ops@emberstack.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EmberStack post-incident readout and remediation roadmap

Hi Lara / EmberStack team,

Attached is our concise post-incident readout covering the Aug 18th inference timeouts you observed. This note includes: a short RCA summary, an annotated timeline (what happened when), immediate mitigations we applied, and our committed remediation roadmap with owners and verification steps.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause: a commit to the KV cache eviction logic in the serving runtime accidentally disabled a guard when a certain sequence-length distribution triggered an edge-case kernel fallback. That resulted in cache fragmentation and repeated cold fetches for long-running sessions, causing per-request token slowdowns and timeouts for 1.8% of EmberStack requests during the window.
- Impact: elevated latency and ~0.7% increase in downstream retries, peaking 08:18-08:46 UTC on Aug 18; no customer data exfiltration detected.
- Immediate mitigation: rolled back the guard and deployed a safe-mode patch at 08:54 UTC; enabled extended KV cache metrics and temporary rate-cap on long sessions.

Key next steps (owners & ETA):
1) Marissa: merge thorough unit + integration tests for eviction logic and kernel fallback (ETA: 2026-09-03).
2) Irene: extended observability — add token-level correlation across KV cache misses in prod for 90-day retention (ETA: 2026-09-10).
3) Sean (ops + accounts): coordinate a verification run with EmberStack and propose a compensated verification window; provide SLA credit calc if agreed (ETA: propose dates by 2026-08-27).

Please see attached: emberstack-rca-summary.pdf (executive summary) and kv-drift-log.txt (anonymized traces).

Request: confirm whether you want us to schedule the verification run the week of Sep 6th — we’ll provide a test plan and runbook. Also let us know if you need a formal SLA credit request template; we’ll prepare it and include the math tied to your contract.

Apologies again for the disruption — we prioritize preventing recurrence and will be transparent on verification.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: emberstack-rca-summary.pdf (pdf), kv-drift-log.txt (text)

Subject: Re: EmberStack post-incident readout and remediation roadmap (technical appendix)

Hi Lara — quick technical appendix to address the KV-key questions and verification shape.

What happened (short technical):
- The eviction guard we shipped was intended to prevent concurrent eviction scans during long-session workloads. Due to a race in the fallback codepath when a quantized kernel was selected, the guard flag was never re-asserted for a small set of sessions that reached >8k tokens across many incremental requests. Those sessions experienced cache fragmentation (multiple smaller segments instead of the expected contiguous slice), which caused the runtime to perform repeated backend fetches and kernel reinitialization.
- The missing KV-key traces you saw are transient: the backend fetchs resolved on the subsequent retry in 98% of cases. For the remaining edge cases where a session saw repeated misses, we have a safe rehydration plan (below).

Mitigation and verification plan (technical):
- Short-term: the safe-mode rollback eliminates the race; we’ve also added a per-session retry limiter to avoid cascading polls.
- Rehydration plan (for any affected sessions): attempt one controlled rehydration for sessions that show >3 consecutive misses; if the job is idempotent we mark it OK; otherwise flag for manual review. We'll provide a script to identify affected job IDs.
- Tests: added a long-session CI job to our nightly matrix and an integration test that simulates the kernel fallback under quantized weights.

Attachments: kv-drift-log.txt (anonymized excerpt), mitigation-plan.md (internal runbook).

Proposed verification windows (we can offer these):
- Sep 7, 09:00–11:00 PDT (low impact for us, avoids EmberStack nightly run)
- Sep 9, 13:00–15:00 PDT (alternate)

If those work I’ll prepare the test harness and a short runbook we can walk through in a 30-minute kickoff.

Marissa
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
